transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-11-07
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (CTO Aurora), Ethan Park (Eng Lead), Lina Gomez (ML Infra), Samir Patel (Security), Olivia Chen (Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
Aurora Infra evaluating Redwood for serving LLMs across hosted and private modes. Key focus: integration with existing SDKs and LangChain/LlamaIndex, gateway/proxy topology, rate limits and quotas, observability hooks (tracing/metrics), and security (VPC, KMS, SOC2). Next steps: Redwood to share pricing and example repo; schedule deep-dive for private network setup.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Priya Rao: Priya here - CTO.
[00:08] Ethan Park: Ethan, engineering lead.
[00:09] Lina Gomez: Lina, ML infra.
[00:11] Samir Patel: Samir, security.
[00:12] Olivia Chen: Olivia, product.
[00:14] Diego Alvarez: Diego, solutions engineer at Redwood.
[00:16] Maya Chen: Great. We'll run through high level, then diego will dive into SDKs/integration patterns. Feel free to interrupt.

[02:05] Priya Rao: High level — we're exploring Redwood because we need predictable latency across our chat and summarization flows. We're deciding between hosted, dedicated, or private. Our concerns are: how intrusive is the integration, does it work with our current LangChain backbone, and how do we enforce quotas per customer?

[02:42] Diego Alvarez: Totally. At a glance, Redwood exposes a simple REST + SDK interface. We have SDKs for Python, Node; we also provide code snippets for LangChain and LlamaIndex adapters. For LangChain, you can swap in the Redwood LLM wrapper with minimal changes — we published a sample repo: github.com/redwood/langchain-examples (note: repo name may be slightly different in transcript).

[03:30] Ethan Park: Quick question — is that a native LangChain connector or more of a shim? Latency sensitive for us, can't add double hop.

[03:45] Diego Alvarez: It's a fairly thin adapter; the SDK uses HTTP/2 streaming and keeps a direct socket to our gateway in hosted mode. On Dedicated/Private, we have an in-cluster runtime that the SDK talks to over gRPC for lower overhead. The LangChain wrapper preserves streaming so you get token-level streaming into your chain. There might be small overhead but not double hop unless you route via a proxy.

[05:10] Lina Gomez: We use LlamaIndex heavily too; is there support there?

[05:18] Diego Alvarez: Yes, we have examples for LlamaIndex. Essentially you implement the LLM interface to call Redwood; embeddings can be done through Redwood's embedding endpoints or your existing vector store. Note: some of our early docs call it Llama-index, the naming in the repo might be inconsistent.

[07:00] Priya Rao: On authentication and networking: if we go Private, we need to keep everything inside our VPC, KMS for keys, and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. How does Redwood handle that?

[07:20] Maya Chen: For Private deployments, we offer an on-prem package with a control plane that can be customer-managed or Redwood-managed in a VPC. KMS integrations supported include AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM options via partners. Audit logs can be exported via syslog or S3 and we have prebuilt connectors for common SIEMs. We'll attach our SOC2 docs and network diagram after.

[09:00] Samir Patel: We need to understand encryption at rest and in transit, and whether KV cache is accessible. Also, what about key rotation?

[09:15] Diego Alvarez: TLS everywhere. KV cache used for prefix caching is encrypted at rest; in Private you control the keys. Key rotation is supported via the KMS integration — it requires a brief restart of the runtime in some configs, but we have zero-downtime rotation patterns for our Dedicated offering. I can share the runbook.

[11:45] Ethan Park: Rate limiting — we need per-tenant quotas and burst controls. Can Redwood enforce quotas at the gateway level?

[12:02] Diego Alvarez: Yes. We expose rate limit policies that can be per-api-key or per-route. Policies support token-based quotas (tokens per minute/hour), concurrent request limits, and burst windows. For Dedicated you can also apply network-level shaping. We also surface backpressure signals in the SDK so your app can fallback gracefully.

[13:30] Olivia Chen: Observability — what hooks do you provide? We need traces, token-level cost breakdown, and per-model metrics.

[13:45] Diego Alvarez: We provide OpenTelemetry-compatible traces, metrics via Prometheus endpoints, and per-request metadata in logs. Token-level cost and latency is available in our Console with per-route breakdowns, and you can export metrics to your existing observability stack. For streaming responses we emit events for start/stop and partial token latencies.

[15:10] Priya Rao: Are there SDK telemetry footprints? We can't have too chatty SDKs from a data governance pov.

[15:20] Diego Alvarez: Telemetry is opt-in for the SDK; by default only essential metrics for retries and errors are collected. In Private, you can disable telemetry altogether.

[17:00] Ethan Park: About gateway/proxy topology — we currently run an edge proxy and would prefer not to route all traffic through a third-party gateway. Can we point the SDK to our gateway and have it forward to Redwood?

[17:20] Diego Alvarez: Yes, you can route requests through your gateway or proxy. In hosted mode that adds a hop and could add latency. For Dedicated/Private we can deploy a local ingress that keeps traffic internal. We also support mutual TLS and client cert auth if you want to secure the path from your gateway to the Redwood runtime.

[19:10] Priya Rao: Wanted to surface cost model — we need guidance whether batching or KV caching will reduce costs for our workload. We have a lot of short prompts and some longer summarizations.

[19:35] Diego Alvarez: Our Optimize tooling analyzes request patterns and suggests batching windows and cache TTLs. For mixed short/long workloads, you often see a 25-40% token-cost reduction with prefix caching plus small batching. We'll run a quick benchmark during a pilot. We'll need a sample traffic trace to simulate.

[21:00] Samir Patel: On compliance: can we get a SOC2 report and penetration test summary? Also need to confirm whether Redwood will sign a DPA and data residency clauses for EU data centers.

[21:20] Maya Chen: Yes to SOC2 and pen-test summary — we'll attach. We do DPAs and offer region pins for EU. For Private you can keep data fully in-region.

[23:45] Olivia Chen: Can you walk through the developer experience for our product team — e.g., switching models, rollouts, canary?

[24:00] Diego Alvarez: Console supports model version pinning, canary rollouts, A/B testing, and automatic fallback policies. You create a route, attach models and traffic splits. We provide SDK flags to target routes. For programmatic control we have APIs to update rollouts.

[26:30] Ethan Park: We have an existing vector DB (Milvus). Embeddings — do we have to use Redwood embeddings or can we continue with our pipeline?

[26:45] Diego Alvarez: You can keep your vector DB. Redwood exposes embeddings endpoints if you want convenience; but it's optional. Many customers call Redwood for generation and continue using their own embedding pipeline.

[29:00] Priya Rao: Pilot timeline — we want a 90-day pilot that tests latency at P50/P95 and cost per 1M tokens. What would Redwood need to start?

[29:20] Maya Chen: For hosted pilot: list of representative prompts, traffic profile (QPS, concurrent requests, typical sequence lengths), and SLO targets. For Dedicated/Private pilot we'll need network topology, access window to spin up a cluster, and a contact for infra. Diego will help scope.

[31:45] Diego Alvarez: I'll also run a LangChain example with your prompt set. The example repo has a notebook and a small harness to replay traffic. It's in the repo link — I'll ping it in the follow-up.

[33:05] Samir Patel: One more on security — audit log formatting and retention, can we push logs to our S3 with lifecycle policies?

[33:18] Diego Alvarez: Yes, logs can be exported to S3 and we support retention policies on export. We also support forwarding to Splunk/Datadog.

[35:00] Olivia Chen: Any known limitations on model size or sequence length in Dedicated or Private?

[35:15] Diego Alvarez: The runtime supports up to very large models; practical limits depend on the GPU profile and quantization. We help pick kernel and quantization profiles. For very long sequences we recommend specific kernel sets; we'll run an evaluation against your longest prompt.

[38:00] Priya Rao: Pricing question again — can you provide committed pricing for Dedicated? We might commit to a 6-month reserved pool.

[38:20] Maya Chen: Yes, we provide reserved pools with monthly or annual commits. We'll send a hosted vs dedicated pricing spreadsheet showing effective unit costs at various commitments.

[40:00] Ethan Park: Operationally — how are upgrades handled in Dedicated? We can't have disruptions mid-quarter.

[40:18] Diego Alvarez: We support rolling upgrades with canary nodes, and a maintenance window that you control in Private/Dedicated. For critical SLOs we can arrange blue/green if needed.

[42:30] Olivia Chen: Are there examples of companies with similar setups?

[42:38] Maya Chen: We can share anonymized case studies for finance and healthcare customers that run Dedicated with private KMS. I'll include links in the follow-up.

[44:00] Priya Rao: Great. Let's summarize next steps.

[44:10] Maya Chen: Summary — Redwood to send: hosted vs dedicated pricing sheet, SOC2 + pen-test summary, network diagram for private deployment, and Diego will share LangChain/LlamaIndex example repo and a small traffic replay harness. Aurora to send: representative prompt set, traffic profile (QPS, concurrent), and compliance checklist. We'll schedule a deep-dive with your infra team next week for private topology.

[46:25] Priya Rao: Sounds good. We prefer early next week for the deep-dive, timezone PST works.

[46:35] Maya Chen: We'll propose two slots in the follow-up. Anything else?

[47:10] Samir Patel: One clarification — when you say telemetry is opt-in, is there a written policy?

[47:20] Maya Chen: Yes, Diego will attach the SDK telemetry policy doc and the exact opt-in flags.

[48:50] Diego Alvarez: I'll also include a small snippet for LangChain that shows token streaming and how to capture partials to your tracing.

[50:00] Olivia Chen: Thanks everyone.
[50:05] Priya Rao: Thanks.
[50:07] Maya Chen: Appreciate your time. We'll follow up with the packet by Friday.
[51:00] Meeting end (recording stopped).

Notes on transcript quality: Automated transcription shows occasional mis-typed product names (LlamaIndex -> Llama-index), and speaker labels may be slightly off in a few places.
